ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening by the incorporating agent, the corporation's bank, and any FINTRAC-reporting intermediary: (i) PEP determination for all directors, officers, significant control persons and authorized signatories under PCMLTFA/PCMLTFR, covering domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, international-organization PEPs, family members and close associates; (ii) screening against Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, including current Canadian sanctions regimes; (iii) OFAC SDN List and OFAC sectoral/country sanctions screening imposed contractually by banks and US/EU civil-infrastructure clients; (iv) UN Security Council Consolidated List verification; (v) negative-news and ownership-structure verification of all direct and indirect UBOs above the 25% statutory threshold; (vi) enhanced due diligence triggers at CA$10,000 cash or high-risk payment-rail thresholds, and assessment of corruption exposure under the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act for civil-infrastructure project awards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (online), ontario.ca/page/business-ontario-registry; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search), nuans.com; federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, corporationscanada.ca.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under OBCA s. 9 and CBCA corporate name provisions, the corporate name must be expressed in English or French using Roman-alphabet letters only; non-Roman scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are prohibited in the formal corporate name, and foreign-language names must be transliterated into Roman characters. The name must contain a distinct element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element (Limited, Ltd., Incorporated, Inc., Corporation, Corp.); the connective 'and' or 'et' is permitted. NUANS pre-search is compulsory for named Ontario corporations; a numbered company (e.g., 1234567 Ontario Limited) may avoid the NUANS filing requirement. Names must not be confusingly similar to existing corporations, trademarks, or names protected under federal or provincial statutes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Engineer / Engineering / Consulting Engineer (Ontario Professional Engineers Act restricted unless Certificate of Authorization is held; avoid for pure CAD/BIM drafting scope)
University / College / Institute / Academy (education licensing restrictions)
Royal / Crown / Government / Police / RCMP / Official
Accountant / Auditor / CPA (Chartered Professional Accountants of Ontario restriction)
Lawyer / Barrister / Solicitor / Legal (Law Society of Ontario prohibition on corporate practice)
Canada / Ontario / municipal geographic tokens implying governmental authority (ministerial consent required)
Certification / Standards / Council tokens implying regulatory or industry-body membership without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon Ontario name rejection: (1) file a fresh NUANS report with an altered distinctive element within the current reservation window; (2) submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Services, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, referencing OBCA s. 9 and Ontario Regulation 62/05, attaching the NUANS report and written legal submissions demonstrating non-confusion and compliance with naming rules; (3) if the Director maintains the refusal, apply to the Ontario Superior Court of Justice under the OBCA's application provisions for an order directing acceptance of the name; (4) extend an approved but unused name reservation by filing an online extension via the Ontario Business Registry before expiry, in further 90-day increments. For a federal CBCA incorporation, the equivalent appeal route is an administrative reconsideration by the Director of Corporations Canada and subsequent judicial review before the Federal Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions: OBCA s. 14 and CBCA s. 19 require a registered office in Ontario or the province of incorporation that is a physical, service-receptive address (no post-office boxes) where corporate records and share registers are kept and legal process can be served. A licensed commercial virtual-office address or a corporate registered-agent address satisfies the Registry if it is a real physical suite with daily mail handling. For a low-risk offshore BIM/CAD drafting entity, virtual-office use is accepted by ServiceOntario and most Canadian banks; however, CRA may scrutinize treaty positions, permanent establishment claims, or HST input tax credits if staffing and records substance is not demonstrable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: LOW but non-zero: estimated annual probability of an unannounced CRA premises inspection is approximately 2%–5% for a service-only, low-risk entity; unannounced registry or municipal verification of the registered office is below 1% absent complaints or registered-agent delisting flags; bank commercial-account KYC reviews are typically documentary rather than physical. The 5% upper bound applies if the company uses a virtual address while claiming CRA business tax credits, HST refunds, or SR&ED incentives in the civil-infrastructure BIM scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 4-6 (incorporation), s. 98 (registered office), s. 115 (directors); O. Reg. 44/01 (filing fees)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario), Ontario Business Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 2) under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Ontario Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account is mandated. Articles may establish authorized share capital with no stated minimum, and a nominal subscription amount (e.g., CAD 1 per common share) may be paid to the corporation upon issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The Corporation hereby adopts its Articles of Incorporation as filed and approved by the Ontario Business Registry; (2) The subscribers' subscriptions for common shares are accepted, and the President shall issue share certificates evidencing the paid-up subscription consideration; (3) The registered office of the Corporation shall be maintained at [address in Ontario], with the President and Secretary appointed as officers having joint management authority; (4) The Secretary shall prepare minutes, share certificates and stated capital records; and (5) Subject to applicable law, all actions taken by the incorporator to effect registration are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario) — name search through authorized NUANS provider or Ontario's online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search for the proposed name through a licensed NUANS provider or the Ontario Business Registry portal. Review conflicting names and protected marks, and obtain a name reservation report. Verify that the name is distinct and does not violate Ontario or federal naming rules.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate name search report (NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, select a slightly amended distinct name and resubmit; appeal to the Registrar for reconsideration under O. Reg. 44/01 if a borderline conflict exists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry — Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 2 (Articles of Incorporation), specifying the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, number and classes of shares, restrictions, and first directors. Submit the form online through the Ontario Business Registry or by mail/courier with the prescribed filing fee and the name search report. Ensure the Initial Notice of Directors and Registered Office (Form 3) is contemporaneously filed where required by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Initial Notice of Directors and Registered Office (Form 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, amend the articles on the registry portal and refile; if rejection is due to incomplete Form 3, immediately file the Initial Notice under s. 115(1) of the OBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Corporation Profile and Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once approved, retrieve the Certificate of Incorporation, Ontario corporation number, and Corporation Profile Report. Verify that the legal name, registered office address, principal place of business, and director details are accurately recorded in the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of data entry errors by filing a Notice of Change with the Ontario Business Registry; pay the correction fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the corporation (Ontario address) — internal corporate action
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator and initial directors convene a directors' meeting to approve the pro-forma first board resolution, adopt the share subscriptions, establish the minute book, issue share certificates, approve the registered office address, and appoint officers. Record all actions in the corporate minute book and maintain the stated capital account in accordance with OBCA record-keeping requirements.
required_dossiers: Minute book, share certificates, and share transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes are defective, hold a subsequent directors' meeting to ratify the original actions and file corrected resolutions in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Tax Registration and CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Ontario Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a CRA business number account and, if required, register for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, payroll contributions, and provincial employer accounts with the Ontario Ministry of Finance. Submit the initial business information return and confirm the registered office address is the same as the CRA correspondence address.
required_dossiers: On-file director list, registered office address, and business activity description (ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330)
GST/HST and payroll registration information if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration, verify the corporation number and business activity classification, correct mismatched data, and resubmit through CRA Business Registration Online.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — knowledge-based CAD/BIM service is not subject to provincial industrial licensing; if the corporation were to provide reserved engineering services to the public, a licence under the Professional Engineers Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. P.28, would be required for the professional engineer.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required for the CAD/BIM business; a Professional Engineering Licence under the Professional Engineers Act may be necessary if the corporation contracts with a licensed professional engineer to supply engineering plans.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable for office-based operations — consider the Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks if the corporation later operates a physical project site or handles hazardous materials.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based drafting and engineering consultancy activities do not trigger an EIA under the Environmental Assessment Act; a Class Screening (Category B) may apply if a client's separate infrastructure project creates environmental consequences.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No intrinsic discharge or emissions from CAD/BIM operations. If leased office premises are used, comply with Ontario Regulation 419/05 (Local Air Quality) for any HVAC or solvent use, and O. Reg. 351/24 (Excess Soil) for construction-related consulting activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require compliance with the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) fire safety certification, Electrical Safety Authority inspection under the Ontario Electrical Safety Code, and workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (O. Reg. 851). No special industrial structural load inspection is applicable to a knowledge-based service office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); principal online portal is My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html); GST/HST returns and registrations filed via GST/HST NETFILE / REGMOR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation automatically obtains a CRA Business Number (BN) at federal or provincial incorporation through the online incorporation linkage; otherwise, Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) is filed with CRA. The 9-digit BN serves as the corporate tax identifier, with Program Accounts: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (payroll), and RM (import/export). Ontario entities incorporated through the Ontario Business Registry receive the BN through CRA's auto-registration linkage. For foreign-entity branches, CRA requires a Form RC1 application, a certificate of existence or equivalent, and appointment of a representative for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Canadian Business Corporation is a separate tax resident liable at the entity level for federal Part I tax (base rate 38% reduced to 15% as the general rate; 9% effective with the small business deduction on first CAD 500,000 if a Canadian-controlled private corporation) plus Ontario corporate income tax (general 11.5%; 10% for manufacturing and processing profits narrowly applied; 3.2% for small business CCDA). Non-resident shareholders bear Part XIII withholding on dividends; the corporation remains the primary taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a check-the-box entity classification regime. Available elections include: (i) GST/HST section 156 election to exclude supplies between closely related corporations; (ii) quick method of accounting election for GST/HST (CRA Form GST74); (iii) federal and provincial section 85 income tax rollover elections for property transfers into a corporation; (iv) hybrid mismatch elections and determinations under ITA sections 94.3-94.7 to neutralize deduction/non-inclusion outcomes; (v) non-resident corporation election under ITA section 216 for rental income; (vi) foreign accrual property income (FAPI) groupings for controlled foreign affiliates under ITA s. 91-95.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) - federal GST at 5% and Ontario provincial component at 8%, combined and administered by CRA as Ontario HST at 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - mandatory registration for a person making taxable supplies in Canada at or above CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); non-resident suppliers providing services relating to Canadian real property or goods are generally deemed to make supplies in Canada and must register even below this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-driven e-invoicing adjudication mandate. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns via GST/HST NETFILE is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1,000,000 (unless a written waiver is granted). PEPPOL-based B2B e-invoicing is available and promoted by the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework but remains voluntary; CRA accepts electronic invoices and documents as valid books and records, which must be retained in readable format for six years from the end of the taxation year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Excise Tax Act (ETA) Schedule VI Part V (services) and Part VI (intangible personal property) for supplies made to a non-resident. Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and structural drafting qualify as zero-rated exports when: (i) the recipient is a non-resident individual or business not registered for GST/HST; (ii) the service is not performed in whole or in part in Canada; (iii) the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada; and (iv) the recipient is outside Canada at the time the service is performed. If drafting/BIM deliverables relate to real property situated in Canada (e.g., Ontario infrastructure stamping or permit drawings), the supply is subject to HST at 13% notwithstanding the non-resident recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Declaration / CAED or Cargo Control Document) - mandatory for physical media or export of goods components; for pure digital BIM/CAD data services, a written statement of no goods export is substituted
Bill of Lading (or contractual delivery receipt / electronic acceptance certificate) proving shipment or offshore delivery of deliverables

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation, Wise/third-party processor transaction statement, or credit advice) evidencing foreign currency inward remittance for the exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export claims retroactively for up to six years (ten years for misrepresentation) and claw back uncollected HST plus arrears interest when non-resident status, foreign performance, or receipt of foreign consideration is not contemporaneously documented. Civil penalties include ETA s. 285 gross negligence (25% of the tax), ETA s. 280 false statements (up to CAD 25,000), and ITA s. 163.2 third-party penalties. Knowingly creating a sham export transaction constitutes tax evasion punishable under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239 by criminal fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years, with corporate directors jointly and severally liable for unremitted HST under ETA s. 323.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank prudential regulation; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF reporting; no separate Canadian foreign-exchange control authority exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; the Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There is no central-bank exchange-control approval for profit remittance, dividend payment, interest repatriation, or capital injection. Repatriation constraints arise only from corporate solvency rules, tax withholding at source, FINTRAC reporting thresholds, and correspondent-bank due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion into CAD, and no stipulated timeline for repatriation of foreign-currency export receipts. Exporters of BIM/CAD services may retain USD/EUR/GBP in permitted bank accounts; cross-border service receipts are reported only for balance-of-payments statistical purposes via Statistics Canada's International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as an ancillary collection and low-value disbursement rail; Low as the primary treasury backbone. Wise Canada and Payoneer act as FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs), not Schedule I chartered banks under the Bank Act. They cannot provide a true demand-deposit bank account with CDIC deposit insurance nor direct Payments Canada membership. They offer borderless multi-currency accounts, virtual account details, and low-cost SWIFT/local-market transfers. Legal constraint: the EMI must be registered as an MSB with FINTRAC before servicing Canadian entities; foreign-owned EMIs should not be used to hold substantial intercompany treasury balances because funds may be pooled or held under trust arrangements rather than as a Canadian bank deposit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Bank Act and PCMLTFA, a bank must identify and verify the corporation, its directors, and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of voting rights. Physical attendance is not a statutory universal mandate, but most Schedule I banks in Ontario require at least one authorized Canadian director or officer to attend an in-branch identity interview with original government-issued photo ID before opening a corporate account with cross-border wire capability. Fully remote opening may be available for simple wholly domestic corporations, but for a foreign-parented CAD/BIM outsourcing vehicle, the strongest onboarding route is in-person execution at a Toronto/Ottawa branch with a board resolution, apostilled company documents, and a completed beneficial-ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent control and offshore engineering delivery model flagged as a potential conduit or shell structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Status, registered office address, complete register of directors and 25%+ beneficial owners, signed board and shareholder resolutions, employment or subcontracting agreements proving local substance, office lease, organizational chart, and two years of projected financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection or large one-time shareholder lending inconsistent with an engineering services company's stated low-risk revenue profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, loan agreement with defined repayment terms, board resolutions, funding-source bank statements, contract pipeline, BIM project purchase orders, invoices with deliverable descriptions, and tax filings demonstrating the funds enter the operating cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP exposure or counterparty red flags in civil-infrastructure contracts, particularly if funds route through multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions and PEP questionnaire, enterprise screening results for directors/counterparties, ultimate beneficial ownership chain of each client and vendor, project-specific contract numbers, public-sector contract references, and a written sanctions-compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern does not match CAD/BIM outsourcing: nominal local employee base but high-value export invoices, back-to-back payments, or significant sub-contractor disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service-level agreements, BIM model tree and BIM 360 audit-trail excerpts, electronic timesheets, fixed-fee/cost-plus work breakdown, HST/GST filings, WSIB and CRA payroll records, and evidence that each invoice reflects documented engineering drafting hours and software usage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or investor to the CA_CORP operating account held at a Schedule I bank in Ontario. Populate field 70 with 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION', 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN', or 'PAYMENT FOR BIM DELIVERABLES', and provide to the receiving bank a board resolution, subscription agreement, and source-of-funds file. Canada imposes no exchange-control prior approval for equity or debt remittance, but the bank must submit a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report for every wire of CAD 10,000 or more. CAD-denominated domestic injection can clear through Lynx; USD injection can clear via Fedwire/CHIPS and settle in the bank's USD correspondent ledger. If the injection constitutes direct investment in a Canadian business, assess whether an Investment Canada Act notification is required and file applicable Statistics Canada balance-of-payments statements if requested.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic subcontractors and vendors in Ontario, use CAD wire via Lynx (wire transfer) or ACSS electronic funds transfer. For cross-border engineering software, platform subscriptions, and foreign technical subcontractors, use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details and remittance-information fields; USD payments settle via Fedwire/CHIPS or through a US clearing agent. For procurement-related infrastructure deliverables where a commercial LC is required by the vendor, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit can be issued against the underlying EPC/BIM service contract, subject to bank collateral and facility approval. Low-value and high-frequency disbursements can be batched through Wise or another FINTRAC-registered MSB for cost efficiency, provided settlement risk is capped by keeping a small float in the fintech wallet only.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward on CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's commercial treasury terms.
FX swaps for short-dated liquidity bridging between CAD and operating foreign currency accounts.
Cross-currency swaps on intercompany shareholder debt to hedge principal and interest flows between CAD and the functional currency of the parent group.
Vanilla FX options on major pairs to protect contingent bids and tender pipelines in civil-infrastructure projects.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where an underlying exposure relates to a non-deliverable emerging-market currency; CAD pairs do not require NDFs because CAD is freely deliverable and convertible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return under the Corporations Information Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (MPBSD) / Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, during the calendar month containing the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 210 late-filing charge applies once the return is more than 60 days overdue; failure to file for three consecutive years authorizes the Director to administratively revoke the certificate of incorporation; revival requires an application, payment of arrears and penalties, and a revival order fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (T2) with supporting schedules and financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the fiscal year-end; tax payment due two months after year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small business deduction, otherwise three months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to a maximum of 12 months; an additional penalty under s. 162(2) applies for a second consecutive late filing; CRA may issue a demand or court order compelling filing, and persistent non-compliance constitutes an offence under s. 238 with concurrent director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Corporations Tax Return (CT23) with applicable schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end, with quarterly instalments while Ontario tax is payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the Ontario tax balance plus 1% per month to a maximum of 12 months; prescribed interest accrues on unpaid balances; chronic non-filing may trigger compliance orders and cancellation of certain provincial tax credits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - applicable only if the entity is federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default of one year after the filing due date, or failure to file for two consecutive years, permits the Director to dissolve the corporation by published notice; revival requires completion of all outstanding filings, settlement of arrears, and payment of the CAD 200 revival fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: OBCA s. 148: mandatory independent audit applies unless waived by unanimous shareholder consent where gross revenues are at or below CAD 500,000 or total assets are at or below CAD 1,000,000; CBCA s. 145: waiver available for non-distributing corporations with gross revenues at or below CAD 1,000,000 or total assets at or below CAD 1,000,000; a licensed public accountant must be appointed at the annual meeting whenever no exemption is available.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private corporations report under Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or may elect full IFRS; publicly accountable entities must apply IFRS; the T2 and CT23 filings must reconcile to the elected accounting framework with statutory adjustments under the Income Tax Act and the Ontario Corporations Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Canada does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership registry. CBCA corporations must keep an individuals-with-significant-control (ISC) register, record changes within 15 days, and confirm its accuracy at each annual filing; Ontario OBCA corporations confirm director and registered-office particulars through the annual Ontario return. Share transfers are not enforceable against the corporation until recorded in the share-transfer register, and false or incomplete ISC entries carry fines up to CAD 200,000 under the CBCA.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 225 - 600 per year (CAD 300 - 800) for a commercial registered office / corporate-agent retainer in Ontario
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,700 - 11,200 per year (CAD 5,000 - 15,000) for a full statutory audit of a small engineering-services private corporation; USD 1,100 - 2,600 for a review engagement where the audit exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Ontario general corporate income tax rate (federal Part I general rate 15% plus Ontario general rate 11.5%). A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment is also subject to Part XIV branch tax at 25%, subject to treaty relief, on after-tax Canadian branch profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday exists in Canada or Ontario. Effective-rate relief is available mainly through: (i) the federal small business deduction and Ontario small business deduction for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation, reducing the combined rate to approximately 12.2% on up to CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income; (ii) Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits, including a refundable 35% ITC for eligible CCPC expenditures; (iii) accelerated capital cost allowance classes for computer software and digital infrastructure; and (iv) foreign tax credit relief for tax paid to a foreign treaty country on the same Canadian-source income. None of these incentives exempt the taxpayer from the obligation to compute and file the T2 return.
